title: Semistable locus and the exceptional-tree local criterion
statement: Let $K$ be a separably closed [def-kun-separably-closed] field [def-weil-field] and $V\subset K$ a valuation ring with fraction field $K$: for every $a\in K^\times$, either $a$ or $a^{-1}$ lies in $V$. Assume that the prime ideals of $V$ form a finite chain, and put $T=\operatorname{Spec}V$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], with generic point $\eta=\operatorname{Spec}K$. Let $(C,D)$ be a multipointed $T$-curve with smooth generic fibre and etale generic marking. Its semistable locus is open in $C$. Suppose $C$ is normal, and $q:(Y,E)\to(C,D)$ is an $\eta$-modification. Let $x\in C$ have image $s\in T$ and be closed in $C_s$, and put $F=q^{-1}(x)$ for the scheme-theoretic inverse image and $Z=F_{\mathrm{red}}$ for its reduced closed subscheme. Suppose $Z$ has pure topological dimension one and every point of $F$ lies in the semistable locus of $(Y,E)$. Then $(C,D)$ is semistable at $x$ if and only if $Z$, after extension to an algebraic closure of $\kappa(s)$, is an exceptional projective-line tree: a connected reduced nodal union of smooth projective lines whose incidence graph is a tree and whose total number of boundary branches in $Y_s$ plus marked points from $E_s$ is at most two. The incidence graph has a vertex for each component and an edge for each node, and a tree is a connected graph without cycles. A boundary branch is a branch of $Y_s$ not belonging to $Z$ that meets $Z$. The tree, its nodes, and its boundary are computed on the reduced subcurve of the semistable source fibre $Y_s$ supported on $F$. The scheme-theoretic fibre $F$ is permitted to have nilpotents and embedded associated points; the assertion concerns its reduced support, not its associated points. Semistable at $x$ means that on a neighbourhood of $x$ the geometric fibres are nodal and the marking is etale over $T$ and disjoint from the relative singular locus. A scheme is normal if every local ring is an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Its normalization means the scheme obtained by taking the integral closure of its structure sheaf in the product of the function fields of its irreducible components; for an integral scheme this is [def-sc-normalization]. A multipointed curve $(X,D)$ over a scheme $T$ means flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] finitely presented [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] morphisms $X\to T$, $D\to T$ of pure relative dimensions $1$, $0$ and a closed immersion $D\hookrightarrow X$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]; $D$ may be empty and $X$ need not be separated or proper over $T$. It is semistable if every singular point of every geometric fibre has completed local ring $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$ over its algebraically closed residue field, $D\to T$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], and $D$ lies in the relative smooth locus [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. For integral $T$ with generic point $\eta$, an $\eta$-modification of multipointed curves is a compatible pair $f_X:X'\to X$, $f_D:D'\to D$ of proper morphisms [def-weil-proper-morphism], each an isomorphism over a schematically dense open and on its generic fibre. A semistable such modification is stable if in each geometric fibre there is no irreducible component isomorphic to $\mathbf P^1$ that is contracted by $f_X$ and meets the union of the marking and the singular points of $X'$ in at most two points. Geometric fibres are [def-weil-geometric-fibre]; dimension is topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]; the local completion is at the maximal ideal [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], and $\Omega[[u,v]]$ denotes the two-variable formal power series ring [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Here an open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow Z$ is schematically dense when $\mathcal O_Z\to j_*\mathcal O_U$ is injective.
